newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian car market blast - 12 reported dead.
newsitem.headline: Algerian car market blast - 12 reported dead.

text.p: A bomb killed 12 people and wounded many others in a car market near the Algerian capital on Thursday, Algerian security forces said.

The explosion ripped through the market, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers, at 10 a.m (0900 GMT). Several of the wounded were in a serious state, security forces said in a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS.

The car market is on the outskirts of Boufarik, an area where Moslem fundamentalist sympathisers are known to live. The market draws thousands of people looking for car bargains on Thursdays, a weekend day in Algeria, residents said.
The official statement did not indicate who was thought to be responsible for the bombing, but security forces have accused Moslem rebels of carrying out similar attacks in the past.
Security forces and rescue service personnel and ambulances rushed to the scene to ferry the wounded to hospitals, the statement said.
Two car bombs killed 20 people and wounded more than 100 eight days ago in Algiers and Ain-Fakroun town, 380 km (240 miles) east of the Algerian capital.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's war between the military-backed government and Islamist rebels since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
Bombings are reported to have killed more than 1,400 people.
